content: 1. Zulkarnain M conducted a study on the prevention of postpartum hemorrhage in West Java, Indonesia. The study was accessed on November 12, 2018. 2. Ejembi C, Shittu O, Moran M, Adiri F, Oguntunde O, Saadatu B, and colleagues investigated the community-level distribution of misoprostol to prevent postpartum hemorrhage during home births in northern Nigeria. Their findings were published in the African Journal of Reproductive Health in 2014, volume 18, issue 2, pages 166-175. 3. Geller S, Carnahan L, Akosah E, Asare G, Agyemang R, Dickson R, and colleagues conducted operations research in rural Ghana to evaluate the community-based distribution of misoprostol for preventing postpartum hemorrhage at home births. The results were published in BJOG in 2014, volume 121, issue 3, pages 319-326. 4. Haver J, Ansari N, Zainullah P, Kim YM, and Tappis H documented their experience with program expansion for the use of misoprostol to prevent postpartum hemorrhage during home births in Afghanistan. Their findings were published in the Journal of Midwifery & Women’s Health in 2016, volume 61, issue 2, pages 196-202. 5. The Mayer Hashi Project focused on preventing postpartum hemorrhage through the community-based distribution of misoprostol in the Tangail District of Bangladesh. This project brief, number 2, was accessed on October 31, 2018. 6. Mir AM, Wajid A, and Gull S conducted a quasi-experimental study to assist rural women in Pakistan in preventing postpartum hemorrhage. Their findings were published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth in 2012, volume 12, article 120. 7. Orobaton N, Abdulazeez J, Abegunde D, Shoretire K, Maishanu A, Ikoro N, and colleagues implemented a large-scale community-based distribution of misoprostol tablets to mothers during the third stage of labor to prevent postpartum hemorrhage in Sokoto State, Nigeria. Early results and lessons learned were published in PLoS One in 2017, volume 12, issue 2, article e0170739. 8. Prata N, Mbaruku G, Grossman AA, Holston M, and Hsieh K examined the safety of community-based availability of misoprostol. Their findings were published in the African Journal of Reproductive Health in 2009, volume 13, issue 2, pages 117-128. 9. Prata N, Gessessew A, Abraha AK, Holston M, and Potts M explored options for preventing postpartum hemorrhage during home births in rural Ethiopia. Their study was published in the African Journal of Reproductive Health in 2009, volume 13, issue 2, pages 87-95. 10. Prata N, Ejembi C, Fraser A, Shittu O, and Minkler M investigated community mobilization efforts to reduce postpartum hemorrhage during home births in northern Nigeria. Their findings were published in Social Science & Medicine in 2012, volume 74, issue 8, pages 1288-1296. 11. Rajbhandari SP, Aryal K, Sheldon WR, Ban B, Upreti SR, Regmi K, and colleagues assessed a program for postpartum hemorrhage prevention in Nepal. Their findings were published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth in 2017, volume 17, article 169. 12. Sibley LM, Spangler SA, Barry D, Tesfaye S, Desta BF, and Gobezayehu AG conducted a regional comparison of distribution strategies and women’s awareness, receipt, and use of misoprostol to prevent postpartum hemorrhage in rural Amhara and Oromiya regions of Ethiopia. Their findings were published in the Journal of Midwifery & Women’s Health in 2014, volume 59, supplement 1, pages S73-S82. 13. Smith JM, Baawo SD, Subah M, Sirtor-Gbassie V, Howe CJ, Ishola G, and colleagues evaluated the advance distribution of misoprostol for postpartum hemorrhage prevention at home births in two districts of Liberia. Their findings were published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth in 2014, volume 14, article 189. 14. Smith JM, Dimiti A, Dwivedi V, Ochieng I, Dalaka M, Currie S, and colleagues studied the advance distribution of misoprostol for postpartum hemorrhage prevention in South Sudan. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Gynaecology & Obstetrics in 2014, volume 127, issue 2, pages 183-188. 15. A country report on the policy and scale-up of misoprostol for postpartum hemorrhage prevention in Madagascar was accessed on October 31, 2018. 16. A country report on the policy and scale-up of misoprostol for postpartum hemorrhage prevention in Mozambique was accessed on October 31, 2018. 17. Webber GC and Chirangi B conducted a pilot study in rural Tanzania to assess the feasibility of providing women with medications to reduce postpartum hemorrhage and sepsis. Their findings were published in Health Care for Women International in 2014, volume 35, issues 7-9, pages 758-770.
